title: E2E tests in staging: simulate SLO breaches and verify auto pause/rollback + audit + suppression
creator: Leila Farouk
description:
Goal
Validate the end-to-end behavior of SLO-driven auto actions (pause + rollback) in staging by generating realistic SLO breaches (latency + error rate) and confirming:
- Rollout controller detects breach via monitor adapter (burn-rate / windows) and takes the configured action.
- Audit trail is emitted with the required fields and is queryable via Console API.
- Suppression controls (admin override + suppression window + “do not rollback during known incident”) work as expected.

Why
We’ve had a few integration spikes where unit tests passed but the system didn’t trigger in practice due to monitor staleness, insufficient sample volume, or scope mismatches (route/model/region/tier). This ticket is the staging gate for enabling the feature on an internal production route.

Test environment
- Target env: staging (us-east-1 + eu-west-1 if time allows)
- Service under test: internal inference route used for canarying rollouts (per ENG-4850 staged enablement plan)
- Feature flags:
  - rollout_controller.slo_evaluator_enabled = true (staging)
  - rollout_controller.auto_rollback_actions_enabled = true (staging)
  - console.auto_actions_api_enabled = true (staging)
- Rollout type(s):
  - Canary (step traffic split: 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50%)
  - A/B baseline vs candidate (fixed split 50/50)

Approach
We’ll implement a staging-only E2E harness that:
1) Creates a rollout scoped to (route, model_version, region, customer_tier) with a known policy template (fast+slow burn windows + min sample + debounce).
2) Generates steady request volume through both baseline + candidate to exceed min sample thresholds for the evaluation windows.
3) Injects failure signals in a controlled way:
   - Latency: introduce an artificial delay for candidate traffic only (e.g., via request header in staging that triggers a sleep in a test shim, or via a staging-only proxy that delays responses).
   - Error rate: force a controlled % of 5xx for candidate traffic only.
4) Verifies decisioning:
   - First phase: expect AUTO_PAUSE at next evaluation boundary (debounce respected).
   - Second phase: once policy is set to rollback-on-breach, expect AUTO_ROLLBACK to last known-good model version / revert traffic split safely.
5) Verifies audit and surfaces:
   - Audit event emitted to event stream with correct correlation IDs.
   - Console API returns the auto-action event with correct fields and timestamps.
   - Links/refs to monitor IDs present (or suppression reason present).
6) Verifies suppression:
   - Admin suppression endpoint prevents rollback and records justification.
   - Suppression window expires and evaluation resumes.
   - “Known incident” override is respected (simulate incident flag on staging).
7) Negative-path tests:
   - Monitor missing: controller should not take auto action; expect “monitor missing/stale” outcome + audit event + metric.
   - Monitor stale: controller should not rollback; expect suppression reason = stale_monitor_data.
   - Low volume: controller should not rollback; expect suppression reason = insufficient_sample.

Instrumentation/verification points
- Metrics:
  - rollout_slo_eval_total{outcome=…}
  - rollout_auto_action_total{action=pause|rollback|suppress,…}
  - rollout_slo_monitor_staleness{…} (if implemented as gauge/counter per standards)
- Logs:
  - rollout-controller decision trace (policy version, monitor IDs, evaluation windows, sample size)
- Data:
  - Console API endpoint for auto actions (ENG-4831) returns events for rollout_id within time window.

Acceptance criteria
- Canary scenario: with injected p99 latency breach on candidate, rollout pauses within <= 10 minutes (depends on window config) and does not advance steps while breached.
- Rollback scenario: with injected error-rate breach on candidate and policy=rollback, traffic returns to baseline and rollout state reflects rollback completion; action is idempotent (no double execution).
- Audit event includes: rollout_id, action, policy_version, monitor_ids (or suppression reason), evaluation_window, sample_size, region, route, model_version, customer_tier, decision_timestamp.
- Suppression scenario: admin suppression prevents rollback, is recorded with justification, and expires correctly.
- Monitor-staleness scenario: system fails safe (no rollback) and emits an explicit “stale/missing monitor” audit outcome + alertable metric.
- Test suite is runnable in CI against staging on demand (manual trigger OK for MVP) and produces a short report with links (Grafana dashboard + rollout detail).

Out of scope
- Multi-region orchestrated failover validation (beyond rollback/pause).
- Quality-eval-based rollback signals.

References
- Design/PRD: Confluence PRD + design spec for SLO integration (see project links in PM-612)
- Related PRs:
  - redwood PR-28490 (staging E2E harness)
  - incident-bot PR-477 (Slack notifications; validate formatting later under ENG-4872)
- Postmortem learnings: 2026-02-17 rollout latency regression gaps (monitor missing/stale) informs negative-path tests.

Owners / reviewers
- Primary: Leila Farouk (E2E automation)
- CI/test infra support: Sahana Iyer
- Eng reviewers: Jada Williams (rollout controller), Chloe Martin (Console backend)
- SRE sign-off: Rafael Mendes / Sean Gallagher (staging scenario + runbook alignment)
acceptance_criteria: Staging canary pauses on latency breach with debounce + min sample enforced (no flapping).
Staging canary rolls back on error-rate breach when policy=rollback; rollback action is idempotent and safe.
Audit trail is emitted and retrievable via Console API; required fields populated.
Admin suppression prevents auto rollback; justification recorded; suppression expires and evaluation resumes.
Missing/stale monitor results in NO rollback + explicit suppress outcome + metric/log/audit visibility.
Suite can be triggered reliably (manual/CI) and outputs links to rollout + dashboards for debugging.
comments: 2026-02-12 (Leila Farouk): Created ticket based on staging-gate requirement from PM-612. Aligning E2E scenarios with burn-rate windows + min sample logic to avoid false positives in staging.

2026-02-14 (Rafael Mendes): Please include a monitor-staleness case. This was the main gap in the 02/17 simulation—controller did nothing, but we had no clear audit signal for why. We need a deterministic suppression reason + alertable metric.

2026-02-18 (Jada Williams): For latency injection, prefer using staging-only header gate in the inference shim (candidate only) rather than messing with telemetry timestamps. Telemetry lag is a separate test (staleness). Also ensure the rollout scope includes customer_tier; we’ve seen mismatches where staging uses default tier and the monitor query doesn’t match.

2026-02-20 (Sahana Iyer): CI note: keep the load generator bounded. We can run as a nightly or manual workflow; avoid long-running tests in the main unit test pipeline. Suggest making the harness accept a duration + target RPS and auto-cleanup rollouts.

2026-02-24 (Leila Farouk): Implementing harness as a single runner: create rollout -> drive load -> inject -> poll controller state -> query Console API -> assert audit events. Drafted assertions for: decision outcome, suppression reason, and rollback completion. Working branch tied to redwood PR-28490.

2026-02-27 (Chloe Martin): Console API endpoint returns events but pagination defaults to 25; the test should query by rollout_id + time window and handle pagination to avoid flakes. Also RBAC: staging test service account needs read:auto_actions permission (see INT-8832).
